instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil.

While it heats, cut the broccoli into small florets, slice the carrots and celery thinly on the diagonal, and cut the bok choy into 1-inch pieces. Slice a quarter of the cabbage and the onion thinly, mince the garlic, and leave the snow peas whole.
Stir the soy sauce and sugar together in a small bowl.
Add the broccoli, carrots and celery to the boiling water and cook for 90 seconds. Lift them out with a strainer into a bowl and leave the water on the heat.
Add the noodles to the same water and cook for 2 minutes, until they're tender but still firm. Drain, rinse under cold water, and drain well.
Heat a large wok or a 12-inch skillet over high heat for 1 minute. Add the oil and the onion and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until the edges start to brown.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells good.
Add the blanched vegetables, snow peas, bok choy and cabbage with the salt. Toss for 2 minutes, until the cabbage wilts but is still crunchy.
Add the noodles and the sauce. Toss with tongs for 2 to 3 minutes, until the noodles are evenly brown. If they stick, add a splash of water.
Take the pan off the heat and tear in half the cilantro. Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash more soy sauce.
Serve topped with the rest of the cilantro.
method_notes: Food.com's Mi Xao Rau Cai (the lead, one review and no rating) is the only version by this name. It steams the harder vegetables, parboils egg noodles, stir-fries onion and garlic in a hot wok, then finishes with soy, sugar and a little fish sauce, which is left out here to keep it vegetarian. Plant Based Jess and Cooking Off the Cuff agree on firm noodles and a soy-based sauce, and add oyster sauce or mushrooms. This version doubles the lead's amounts for 4, and blanches the vegetables in the noodle water to save a pot. It is dairy-free, nut-free and vegetarian.
